topics.title: The sine rule and the area formula

questions.stem: A surveyor walks from post \(A\) to post \(B\), then to post \(C\), and finally back to \(A\). \(B\) is \(80\text{ km}\) north of \(A\), and the bearings of \(C\) from \(A\) and \(B\) are \(045^{\circ}\text{T}\) and \(072^{\circ}\text{T}\) respectively. Find the total distance walked, correct to the nearest kilometre.
questions.hint: Draw the triangle and find the interior angles. Then use the sine rule to find the other two sides.
questions.solution: Let the vertices of the triangle be \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\). Side \(AB = 80\text{ km}\). Angle \(A\) (angle \(BAC\)) is \(45^{\circ}\) because the bearing is \(045^{\circ}\) from North. At \(B\), the bearing of \(C\) is \(072^{\circ}\). Since the line \(AB\) goes south to north, the angle \(ABC\) inside the triangle is \(180^{\circ} - 72^{\circ} = 108^{\circ}\). Then angle \(C = 180^{\circ} - 45^{\circ} - 108^{\circ} = 27^{\circ}\). By the sine rule: \(\frac{AC}{\sin 108^{\circ}} = \frac{80}{\sin 27^{\circ}} \implies AC = \frac{80 \sin 108^{\circ}}{\sin 27^{\circ}} \approx 167.58\text{ km}\). And \(\frac{BC}{\sin 45^{\circ}} = \frac{80}{\sin 27^{\circ}} \implies BC = \frac{80 \sin 45^{\circ}}{\sin 27^{\circ}} \approx 124.59\text{ km}\). Total distance = \(AB + BC + AC \approx 80 + 124.59 + 167.58 = 372.17 \approx 372\text{ km}\).

steps.explain: Draw a diagram. Since B is due North of A, the bearing from A to C (045°) means the interior angle \(\angle BAC = 45^{\circ}\).
The bearing from B to C is 072°. Because B is due North of A, the line AB lies on the North-South line. The angle inside the triangle at B is supplementary to the bearing.
Use the Sine Rule to find BC.
Use the Sine Rule to find AC.
